page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Catenation is the linking of atoms of the
same element to one another by covalent
The atoms may join into straight chains,
A chain of carbon atoms, C–C–C–C, is the
steps.why: The word means self-linking: the bond that counts is between two atoms of the same element, not between the element and oxygen or hydrogen. Naming chains and rings together keeps the definition complete, because catenation covers both.
common_mistakes: Defining catenation as the linking of any two atoms. The atoms joined must be atoms of the same element.
Writing that catenation gives chains only. Rings come from the same self-linking and count as catenation.
steps.memory_tip: Catena means a chain: catenation is a chain of atoms of one element.
steps.margin_note: Say same element and covalent bond; both words carry the definition.

Silicon and sulphur also catenate, but
steps.why: The strength of the bond between two atoms of the element is what limits catenation: a strong C–C bond keeps a long chain together, while the weaker Si–Si and Ge–Ge bonds break more easily and their chains stay short. That one bond energy is the reason carbon has more compounds than any other element.
common_mistakes: Giving the small size and stopping there. Small size is a real reason, but say how it works: the small carbon atoms make the strong C–C bond of 348 kJ mol⁻¹, and that bond is what holds a long chain together.
Naming carbon as the only element that catenates. Silicon and sulphur do as well, though to a much smaller extent.
steps.memory_tip: The stronger the bond between atoms of the same element, the longer the chain: C–C at 348 kJ mol⁻¹ is the strongest.
steps.margin_note: One number, the C–C bond energy, turns the definition into a reason.

insider_note: A definition on its own is short for this question. Add the element that shows catenation best and the bond energy that explains it, and the answer is complete.
